title: A picture for every idea
when: A finance, benefits or business conversation where the guest explains things (rules of thumb, numbers, how something works) and the clip goes to social feeds.
story: Open on the question the host asks; let each of the guest's ideas land as its own picture; close on the line worth repeating.
picture: Every guest line gets a small drawing of its idea (a sketch with its numbers, a cast object, tiles that count months, a jar, a mug with the quote on it); host lines stay short poster type; readable pop captions run under everything with the speaker's chip; one or two objects come back across the clip.
pace: Cut when the thought changes, not on every sentence; hold a picture while its idea is being explained; never let type change faster than it can be read.
rules: Keep the recording as recorded; pictures follow the words, never the other way round.
Attribute rules of thumb to the speaker in one short line ("Sam, on air"), not with disclaimers.
Pictures carry the idea; captions carry the words. Kinetic type only for the line worth repeating.
Draw the guest's own examples (their numbers, their objects) rather than stock metaphors.

examples/podcast-pictures shows it end to end: the recording imported as recorded, then a picture for each idea the guest explains (casts of the guest's own objects, a chart for the figures), one kinetic line, and captions below the pictures.
